lessons.title: The Problem: Managing Guest Connectivity Without a Tool
lessons.content:
## The status quo — and why it hurts

On a cruise ship or superyacht, dozens or hundreds of guests and crew members connect to the onboard network every day. Without a dedicated management tool, every request — "my internet isn't working," "can you change my plan," "I need extra bandwidth for a video call" — lands on the ETO or IT officer. They have to log into a backend system, contact the NOC, or wait for shore-side support. Guests wait. Crew frustration grows.

For a boutique cruise operator, this creates a real operational problem: hotel staff (front desk, guest relations) are the first line of contact for guests, but they have no visibility into the network — they can't answer basic questions, let alone fix anything. The ETO becomes a helpdesk for issues that shouldn't require a network engineer.

## Where Unity Local Admin fits

Unity Local Admin is a set of dashboards built directly into the **UNITY platform** — OmniAccess's single management interface for all onboard digital services. It is the **guest access management** layer of the Captive Portal: the tool that lets on-vessel staff monitor every connected user, adjust access, and onboard new guests — all from a single browser-based screen, without backend access or technical training.

In the OmniAccess portfolio map it sits under **Network — NaaS**, specifically in the **Captive Portal** capability. It's not a separate product to sell — it's the operator-facing control layer that makes the Captive Portal manageable on a day-to-day basis by the people who are actually on board.

## Who benefits most

| Persona | The frustration it removes |
|---|---|
| ETO / IT Officer | No longer the manual helpdesk for every connectivity question |
| Hotel Manager / Front Desk | Can see, create and adjust guest accounts without calling IT |
| Captain | Fewer complaints escalated to the bridge; visible, managed experience |
| IT Fleet Manager | Fleet-wide consistency in how guest access is provisioned and monitored |

## A sentence you can use

"Unity Local Admin gives your hotel team and ETO a single screen where they can see every connected guest and crew member, fix common issues instantly, and onboard hundreds of guests in minutes — without involving shore-side support."

## Discovery questions

- "Today, when a guest reports a connectivity problem, who handles it — and how long does it take?"
- "Can your hotel staff currently see which guests are connected and how much of their data allowance they've used?"
- "How do you currently onboard guest internet access at the start of a cruise?"

lessons.title: The Dashboard: What You See and What You Can Do
lessons.content:
## One screen, full picture

The core of Unity Local Admin is the **Accounts dashboard** — a live list of every guest and crew member connected on the vessel. At a glance, hotel staff or the ETO can see:

- **Name and room number** — who is connected and where they are staying.
- **User type and tier** — Guest (Standard Room or VIP Room) or Crew (Regular Crew or Crew Executive).
- **Profile** — the specific connectivity package applied to that user (defines their data quota and how many devices they can connect).
- **Booking start and end date** — so staff can spot expired accounts before a guest does.

With a click on the **detail view** for any user, staff get a deeper picture: current data usage (quota used vs. total), which devices are connected, recent app traffic over the past 48 hours, account status (active or blocked), and the exact profile being applied. They can take action directly from this screen.

## User types and tiers: the access structure

The system organises access into two dimensions:

**User types:** Guest and Crew. Each type has two tiers:
- Guest: **Standard Room** and **VIP Room**
- Crew: **Regular Crew** and **Crew Executive**

Each tier has a default **profile** — a pre-configured package that defines data quota and maximum number of devices. For example, a VIP Room guest might have a larger quota than a Standard Room guest, and a Crew Executive gets more data than Regular Crew.

These profiles are not locked — they can be adjusted per user, giving operators the flexibility to offer differentiated service tiers (think "premium connectivity" as an upsell) without requiring a technical configuration change.

## For the seller: how to frame this

- **To an IT Fleet Manager:** "Every account, every quota, every device — visible in one place, with a consistent structure across your fleet."
- **To a Captain:** "Your hotel team can answer connectivity questions themselves. Guests don't come to the bridge."
- **To an Owner's Rep on a superyacht:** "Owner and family accounts can be set up with a dedicated tier — full visibility, private, separate from crew."

⚠️ **Important:** The Purchases and Consolidations dashboards that appear in the navigation menu **do not work** in the current version (Unity 4.1.8). If a prospect asks about billing or package-purchase features, be clear that those dashboards are not yet functional. Do not position them as available capabilities.

lessons.title: Creating and Removing Users: The Operational Freedom Story
lessons.content:
## The core operational question: how do guests get on?

Every cruise or charter starts with the same challenge: getting guests connected quickly. Unity Local Admin offers three methods for creating user accounts, each suited to a different scenario. Understanding these lets you tell a compelling story about operational efficiency.

## Method 1 — Create by Room

The simplest method for individual guests. Staff enter a first name, last name, room number, and booking dates, then select user type and tier. The system automatically generates a login credential. No passwords to manage, no usernames to invent. Ideal for: hotel desk staff onboarding individual late arrivals or crew members who join mid-voyage.

**Seller's angle:** "Your front desk can check in a late arrival and have them connected in under a minute."

## Method 2 — Create by Voucher

Staff manually set a username and password and associate the account with a room and booking window. The admin controls the login credential explicitly. Ideal for: situations where the guest or manager wants a specific, memorable login (e.g., for a family cabin or a repeat VIP).

**Seller's angle:** "Full control over who gets what access, set up exactly how the hotel wants it."

## Method 3 — Bulk Voucher Creation

This is the headline operational story. Staff enter a login prefix, a quantity, and booking dates — the system generates a full batch of username/password combinations in one step and exports them as a **downloadable CSV file**. The Hotel Manager can distribute the CSV directly to guests (or download it themselves).

In practice: a 200-guest sailing can be fully onboarded — every account created, credentials ready to hand out — in minutes, before guests even board.

**Seller's angle:** "Your hotel team can onboard an entire sailing's worth of guests in one go, without a single call to IT."

⚠️ **Important limitation to know:** There is a current bug in Bulk Voucher creation where the Login Prefix must be entered in **lowercase letters**. Uppercase characters cause the process to fail. This is an active issue that operators need to be aware of.

## Deleting users

When a guest departs or an account needs to be removed, the Delete User action removes the record completely from the system. This is a permanent action — it clears the user from the Captive Portal database entirely. Useful for: end-of-cruise cleanup, or removing an account that was created in error.

## Putting it together: the self-service story

Across all three creation methods, there is one consistent message: **hotel staff can manage guest connectivity end-to-end without IT involvement**. Whether it's a single arrival, a custom VIP credential, or a full-sailing batch, the Hotel Manager has the tools to handle it from the Unity dashboard.

lessons.title: Positioning Across Personas
lessons.content:
## The same capability, different stories

Unity Local Admin is one tool, but the value story changes depending on who you're talking to. Here is how to adapt your message.

## IT Fleet Manager / IT Director (large cruise fleets)

This persona's world is fleet-wide consistency, OPEX predictability, and keeping the NOC from being overwhelmed by trivial requests.

**Story to tell:** "Unity Local Admin gives your teams a standardised, role-based management layer across every vessel. User types, tiers, and profiles are configured consistently — your hotel staff work the same way on Ship A as on Ship B. And because they can handle routine requests themselves, your NOC isn't fielding calls every time a guest's password doesn't work."

**Discovery questions:**
- "How many support tickets per sailing relate to basic guest connectivity issues?"
- "Do your hotel teams currently have any self-service tools for managing guest internet access?"

## Captain (smaller vessels, direct decision-maker)

The Captain cares about the vessel running smoothly and guests being happy — without problems arriving at the bridge.

**Story to tell:** "When a guest walks up to the front desk about their wifi, your hotel team fixes it on the spot. They see the account, they see the usage, they can change the profile or reset access. It doesn't come to you."

**Discovery question:**
- "When there's a guest connectivity complaint today, who does it end up with?"

## ETO / IT Officer (technical influencer, daily user)

This persona lives with the product every day. They need it to be simple enough for hotel staff to use without calling them, and they need visibility without having to dig into backend systems.

**Story to tell:** "You stay out of the routine stuff. Hotel staff can see and manage guest accounts. You get the dashboard when you need it — quota, devices, app traffic — but you're not the first call every time a guest can't remember their password."

**Discovery question:**
- "How much of your time today goes on connectivity requests that hotel staff could theoretically handle themselves if they had the right tool?"

## Owner's Representative / Superyacht context

On a superyacht, privacy, discretion, and a seamless owner experience are paramount. The ETO must never be caught flat-footed.

**Story to tell:** "The owner's connectivity is its own tier. You can set it up separately — dedicated profile, private quota — and you have full visibility to proactively spot any issue before it becomes a conversation. No surprises."

**Discovery question:**
- "Is owner and family connectivity currently managed separately from crew and guest access?"

lessons.title: Objections and What to Know Before You Walk In
lessons.content:
## Common objections — and how the product responds

### 'We already have a Captive Portal — why do we need another layer?'

Unity Local Admin is not a separate product competing with the Captive Portal — it is the management interface that makes the Captive Portal usable by on-vessel operations staff. Without it, the Captive Portal is a backend system that only the NOC or a technical officer can interact with. Unity Local Admin brings that control to the people on the vessel who need it every day.

### 'Our ETO handles connectivity — we don't need hotel staff involved.'

This is actually the problem Unity Local Admin solves. If the ETO is the single point of contact for every guest connectivity issue, that's a risk: when the ETO is unavailable (off-watch, focused on critical systems), guests wait and complaints accumulate. Unity Local Admin distributes the capability without distributing the complexity.

### 'We're worried about hotel staff making mistakes on the network.'

The dashboard provides access-level controls appropriate to hotel operations (account creation, profile changes, account deletion) — it does not expose network configuration or routing. Hotel staff cannot accidentally reconfigure the network; they work within the access management layer only.

### 'Is this available now, or is it a roadmap item?'

Unity Local Admin is operational and available from Unity version 4.1.8. It is not a roadmap item — it is in production use today.

## What to know: active limitations

Two limitations are important to be transparent about before a customer goes live:

1. **Purchases and Consolidations dashboards are not functional** in Unity 4.1.8. These tabs appear in the navigation but do not work. If a customer expects in-system package purchasing or financial consolidation reporting, that capability is not currently available.

2. **Bulk Voucher: Login Prefix must be lowercase.** There is an active bug where using uppercase letters in the bulk voucher Login Prefix causes the process to fail. Operations teams need to be briefed on this before their first sailing batch.

## What is missing from the source (for the team)

The technical documentation does not include:
- Pricing or packaging information for Unity Local Admin as a feature or add-on.
- Customer case studies or live deployment examples.
- A roadmap for the Purchases/Consolidations fix or other upcoming features.
- Integration details with PMS (Property Management Systems) or booking platforms.

These would strengthen the sales conversation and should be gathered from Product or Customer Success before customer-facing demos.

lessons.title: Cheat Sheet: Unity Local Admin in One Page
lessons.content:
## Elevator pitch (1–2 sentences)

Unity Local Admin is the onboard management interface for guest and crew connectivity — built into the UNITY platform. It gives hotel staff and ETOs full visibility over every connected user and the ability to onboard, adjust, or remove accounts in real time, without involving shore-side IT.

---

## Key benefits by persona

| Persona | What to say |
|---|---|
| IT Fleet Manager | Fleet-wide consistent access structure; hotel teams self-serve routine requests; fewer NOC interruptions. |
| Captain | Connectivity complaints resolved at the desk, not on the bridge. |
| ETO / IT Officer | Full dashboard visibility (quota, devices, app traffic) with hotel staff handling the routine workload. |
| Hotel Manager | Create one guest or 200 guests in minutes; hand out credentials as a CSV; no IT call needed. |
| Owner's Rep (superyacht) | Owner's party on a dedicated tier with private quota — proactive visibility, no surprises. |

---

## Discovery questions

1. "When a guest reports a connectivity problem today, who handles it — and how long does it take?"
2. "Can your hotel staff currently see which guests are connected or how much of their allowance is left?"
3. "How do you onboard guest internet access at the start of a sailing?"
4. "How much of your ETO's time goes on connectivity requests that hotel staff could handle with the right tool?"
5. "Is owner/family connectivity currently managed separately from crew and general guest access?"

---

## Active limitations to know

- **Purchases and Consolidations dashboards are not functional** in Unity 4.1.8 — visible in the UI but not operational. Do not present as available features.
- **Bulk Voucher: Login Prefix must be lowercase** — an active bug causes the process to fail if uppercase letters are used.

---

## Natural next step

Request a guided demo of the Unity dashboard showing the Accounts view, the per-user detail panel, and a live Bulk Voucher creation. Involve the ETO and Hotel Manager together — they are the day-one users and the sharpest validators of the workflow story.

---

## Where it sits in the portfolio

Unity Local Admin is part of **Network — NaaS / Captive Portal**, delivered through the **UNITY platform**. It does not require additional hardware. It becomes available from **Unity version 4.1.8**.

answers: It is a standalone product sold separately from the UNITY platform, requiring its own hardware appliance.
It is part of the Connectivity / Fusion portfolio — a management layer for multi-orbit satellite plans.
It is the operator-facing management interface for the Captive Portal, delivered as part of the UNITY platform under Network — NaaS.
It is part of the Cybersecurity portfolio, providing access control aligned with the NIST framework.
questions.explanation: Unity Local Admin is a dashboard within the UNITY platform, specifically for managing the Captive Portal (guest access). It sits under Network — NaaS in the OmniAccess portfolio map, not under Connectivity or Cybersecurity.
